# 1. Introduction

Flight operations generate large amounts of data related
to airlines, airports, flight schedules, delays and
travel distances.

This project focuses on analysing flight records using
R Programming. It aims to identify patterns in airline
performance, airport traffic and flight delays through
data analysis and visualization.

## 1.1 Problem Statement

Raw flight datasets contain information that can be
difficult to understand without proper analysis.

This project uses R Programming to clean, analyse and
visualize flight data to identify important patterns
and understand flight operational performance.

## 1.2 Objectives

The main objectives of this project are:

- To analyse flight records and identify overall flight activity.
- To compare the performance of different airlines.
- To identify the busiest origin and destination airports.
- To analyse departure and arrival delays.
- To study flight status distribution.
- To identify monthly and weekday flight trends.
- To visualize flight information using statistical charts.
- To develop an interactive and professional analytical report.

## 1.3 Dataset Information

The project uses a flight dataset containing 1,000
records and 11 original columns.

The dataset includes information about:

- Flight identification
- Flight date
- Airline name
- Origin airport
- Destination airport
- Scheduled departure time
- Actual departure time
- Departure delay
- Arrival delay
- Flight distance
- Flight status

The dataset contains simulated flight records and is
used for academic analysis and visualization.

# 2. Install and Load Packages

R Programming provides several packages for data
manipulation, statistical analysis and visualization.

The following packages will be used in this project.
```{r}
packages <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "dplyr",
  "tidyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "readr",
  "lubridate",
  "knitr",
  "DT",
  "plotly"
)

new_packages <- packages[
  !(packages %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])
]

if(length(new_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(new_packages)
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(knitr)
```
## 2.1 Packages Used

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| tidyverse | Data manipulation |
| dplyr | Data analysis |
| tidyr | Data cleaning |
| ggplot2 | Data visualization |
| readr | CSV file import |
| lubridate | Date and time analysis |
| plotly | Interactive charts |
| DT | Interactive data tables |
| knitr | Report generation |

# 3. Import Dataset
The flight dataset is imported into R using the read_csv() function from the readr package.
```{r}
flights <- readr::read_csv("flights-1000.csv")
head(flights)
```

## 3.1 Dataset Structure
The structure of the dataset is examined to understand its columns and data types.
```{r}
str(flights)
```

cat("Number of Rows:", nrow(flights))
cat("\nNumber of Columns:", ncol(flights))

Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is used to

cat("Total Rows:", nrow(flights))

head(flights)

# 5. Data Cleaning and Transformation

Data cleaning is performed to improve data quality,
handle missing values and prepare the dataset for analysis.

## 5.1 Convert Data Types
```{r}
flights$flight_date <- as.Date(flights$flight_date)

flights$airline <- as.factor(flights$airline)
flights$origin <- as.factor(flights$origin)
flights$destination <- as.factor(flights$destination)
flights$status <- as.factor(flights$status)

str(flights)
```

## 5.2 Create New Columns
```{r}
flights <- flights %>%
  mutate(
    month = lubridate::month(flight_date, label = TRUE),
    weekday = lubridate::wday(flight_date, label = TRUE)
  )

head(flights)
```

## 5.3 Missing Values After Cleaning
```{r}
missing_after_cleaning <- data.frame(
  Column = names(flights),
  Missing_Values = colSums(is.na(flights))
)

knitr::kable(
  missing_after_cleaning,
  caption = "Missing Values After Data Preparation"
)
```

## 5.4 Data Type Verification
```{r}
data_types <- data.frame(
  Column = names(flights),
  Data_Type = sapply(flights, function(x) class(x)[1])
)

knitr::kable(
  data_types,
  caption = "Dataset Column Data Types"
)
```

## 5.5 Final Dataset Overview
```{r}
cat("Total Records:", nrow(flights))
cat("\nTotal Columns:", ncol(flights))
cat("\nDuplicate Records:", sum(duplicated(flights)))
```

# 6. Data Visualization

Data visualization helps identify patterns and trends
in airline operations and airport activities.

## 6.1 Airline-wise Flight Distribution
```{r}
airline_count <- flights %>%
  count(airline, name = "Total_Flights")

ggplot(airline_count,
       aes(x = reorder(airline, Total_Flights),
           y = Total_Flights,
           fill = airline)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Flight Distribution by Airline",
    x = "Airline",
    y = "Total Flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## 6.2 Average Departure Delay by Airline
```{r}
airline_delay <- flights %>%
  group_by(airline) %>%
  summarise(
    Average_Delay = mean(dep_delay_min, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

ggplot(airline_delay,
       aes(x = reorder(airline, Average_Delay),
           y = Average_Delay,
           fill = airline)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Average Departure Delay by Airline",
    x = "Airline",
    y = "Average Delay (Minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## 6.3 Top 10 Busiest Origin Airports
```{r}
airport_traffic <- flights %>%
  count(origin, name = "Total_Flights") %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Flights)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

ggplot(airport_traffic,
       aes(x = reorder(origin, Total_Flights),
           y = Total_Flights,
           fill = Total_Flights)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Busiest Origin Airports",
    x = "Origin Airport",
    y = "Total Flights",
    fill = "Flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 6.4 Flight Status Distribution
```{r}
status_analysis <- flights %>%
  count(status, name = "Total_Flights")

ggplot(status_analysis,
       aes(x = status, y = Total_Flights, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = Total_Flights),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Flight Status",
    x = "Flight Status",
    y = "Number of Flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## 6.5 Monthly Flight Trends
```{r}
monthly_flights <- flights %>%
  count(month, name = "Total_Flights")

ggplot(monthly_flights,
       aes(x = month, y = Total_Flights, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "darkblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = Total_Flights),
    vjust = -0.8,
    size = 3
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Flight Activity",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Total Flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 7. Statistical Analysis and Key Insights
## 7.1 Airline Performance Analysis

```{r}
airline_performance <- flights %>%
  group_by(airline) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Flights = n(),
    Average_Departure_Delay = round(
      mean(dep_delay_min, na.rm = TRUE), 2
    ),
    Average_Arrival_Delay = round(
      mean(arr_delay_min, na.rm = TRUE), 2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Flights))

knitr::kable(
  airline_performance,
  caption = "Airline Performance Analysis"
)
```

## 7.2 Airport Traffic Analysis
```{r}
airport_analysis <- flights %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Departures = n(),
    Average_Delay = round(
      mean(dep_delay_min, na.rm = TRUE), 2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Departures))

knitr::kable(
  head(airport_analysis, 10),
  caption = "Top 10 Airports by Departure Traffic"
)
```

## 7.3 Overall Flight Statistics
```{r}
overall_statistics <- flights %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Flights = n(),
    Average_Departure_Delay = round(
      mean(dep_delay_min, na.rm = TRUE), 2
    ),
    Average_Arrival_Delay = round(
      mean(arr_delay_min, na.rm = TRUE), 2
    ),
    Average_Distance_KM = round(
      mean(distance_km, na.rm = TRUE), 2
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  overall_statistics,
  caption = "Overall Flight Statistics"
)
```

# 8. Key Findings

The analysis of the flight dataset provides the following
important observations:

- The dataset contains 1,000 simulated flight records.
- Flight status analysis helps compare on-time, delayed,
  cancelled and diverted flights.
- Airline performance analysis compares flight volumes
  and average departure and arrival delays.
- Airport traffic analysis identifies the busiest
  origin airports.
- Monthly analysis highlights changes in flight activity.
- Data quality analysis identifies missing values and
  duplicate records.
  
# 9. Conclusion

The SkyTrack project demonstrates how R Programming
can be used for flight data analysis and visualization.

The project covers data importing, data cleaning,
exploratory data analysis, statistical analysis and
graphical representation.

The visualizations and analytical tables help understand
airline activity, airport traffic, flight delays and
monthly flight trends.

This project provides practical experience in using
R packages such as dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, lubridate
and plotly.

Since the dataset contains simulated records, the
findings are intended for academic analysis and do
not represent actual airline performance.
